summary.en: Abdul El-Sayed, a former public health official, secured the Democratic nomination in Michigan's Senate race, defeating congresswoman Haley Stevens. He celebrated his victory as a triumph over significant external financial influence.

This reminds us that true authority and promotion ultimately rest with Yahweh, who raises up and brings down leaders according to His will. Such moments encourage us to look beyond visible forces and trust in...

title.en: Trump is pioneering the role of commentator-in-chief when issues grow thorny
title.zh: 当问题变得棘手时，特朗普正在开创“首席评论员”的角色

summary.en: The article describes how the president has adopted a role akin to a chief commentator, consistently interpreting events, labeling individuals as heroes or villains, and guiding public opinion on complex issues.
summary.zh: 文章指出，总统正在开创一种“首席评论员”的角色，不断地为事件赋予动机，划分英雄与反派，并引导公众对棘手问题形成看法。

body.en: The president is constantly assigning motives, identifying heroes and villains, and telling his audience what to think This was originally published in This Week in Trumpland. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday From Charles Barkley to Thierry Henry to John McEnroe, the path from the arena to the commentary box is well trodden , and plenty of politicians have made the transition from elected office to the TV studio. One man, however, insists on doing both at the same time. Donald Trump is the US president, empowered to kill terrorists, grant pardons, sign and veto bills, and represent the nation on the world stage. But when issues become thorny, as they have of late, he is wont to embrace an alternative role as commentator-in-chief. Continue reading...
body.zh: 总统不断地分配动机，识别英雄和恶棍，并告诉他的听众该怎么想。这最初发表在《特朗普乐园的本周》上。注册后每周三都会在收件箱中收到它 从查尔斯·巴克利到蒂埃里·亨利再到约翰·麦肯罗，从竞技场到评论室的道路已经被人熟知，许多政客已经从民选办公室过渡到电视演播室。然而，有一个人坚持同时做这两件事。唐纳德·特朗普是美国总统，有权杀死恐怖分子、给予赦免、签署和否决法案，并在世界舞台上代表国家。但当问题变得棘手时，就像最近发生的那样，他习惯于接受首席评论员的替代角色。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In an age where powerful voices constantly shape narratives, it's easy to accept the first interpretation of events. Proverbs 18:17 reminds us that a case always seems right until another perspective is heard and examined. This calls us to seek out diverse viewpoints and engage in thoughtful discernment, rather than passively accepting pre-assigned labels.
reflection.zh: 在一个强大的声音不断塑造叙事的时代，我们很容易接受对事件的第一种解读。雅伟的话语提醒我们，先陈述案情的人似乎有理，直到有人前来查问。这呼吁我们寻求多元的观点，进行审慎的辨别，而不是被动地接受预设的标签。

verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: Left-wing political outsider wins Democratic Senate primary in Michigan
title.zh: 左翼政治局外人赢得密歇根州民主党参议员初选

summary.en: Abdul El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, has won the Democratic Senate primary in Michigan. If elected in November, he would become the first Muslim US senator.
summary.zh: 埃及移民之子阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德赢得了密歇根州民主党参议员初选。如果他在11月当选，他将成为美国首位穆斯林参议员。

body.en:
Left-wing political outsider Abdul El-Sayed is projected to win Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, a race that exposed bitter divisions within the party over its future direction.

The former public health official is on track to narrowly beat moderate Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

"In the words of Mohammad Ali, 'We shook up the world,'" El-Sayed said, quoting the famed boxer's declaration after his underdog defeat of Sonny Liston in 1964.

He will face Republican and Trump ally Mike Rogers, in November's midterm elections. If elected, El-Sayed would become the first Muslim to serve in the US senate.

The final result was much closer than El-Sayed's camp had expected, with fewer than 15,000 votes - a margin of just under 1 percentage point out of more than 1.5 million ballots counted - separating him from Stevens as of late Wednesday morning.

"The movement to get money out of politics, put money in your pocket, and pass Medicare for All is a big movement," El-Sayed said on Wednesday, echoing a familiar refrain he had used on the campaign trail.

"I want to congratulate Abdul El-Sayed on winning the Democratic nomination for US Senate," Stevens said in a statement. "He is a doctor, a community health official, a Rhodes Scholar, and a dedicated Michigander. I am proud to offer my support as he takes on Mike Rogers in the general election."

The November midterm elections will determine the balance of power in Washington for the last two years of President Donald Trump's time in office.

Trump declared the Michigan Senate result "Great news for the Republican Party".

In his post on Truth Social, Trump referred to the Democratic Party as the "Dumocrats", and claimed their "crazy policies will only get worse!"

After a bruising and sometimes bitter campaign, El-Sayed hinted at bridge-building when he addressed supporters on Tuesday night, before the outcome was known.

"Whatever happens tonight, we have a responsibility to ensure that we unite, unite to make sure that [Republican] Mike Rogers never sees the inside of the US Senate."

El-Sayed, who was endorsed by left-wing politicians including Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders and New York City congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, has voiced support for progressive causes like universal healthcare and abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Stevens, 43, took a more moderate approach, pitching herself as the middle-of-the-road candidate who would appeal to voters unsure of which party to back in November. She made a promise to save manufacturing jobs in Michigan, should she be elected.

Stevens earned the endorsement of Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer, as well as outgoing Senator Gary Peters.

title.en: Drone carrying explosives found at German airport, police say
title.zh: 警方称德国机场发现携带爆炸物的无人机

summary.en: The drone was found near Ukrainian cargo planes before another object collided with a cargo aircraft in mid-air.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A drone carrying an explosive device has been found at a German airport, police say.

A robot was deployed at Leipzig/Halle Airport after the device was spotted by an employee near Ukrainian cargo planes overnight, according to Saxony police.

A second unidentified object also collided with a cargo aircraft near the same airport. Minor damage was detected on the aircraft after it landed in Hanover.

German airports are on high alert following a series of unauthorised drone flights in recent months over sensitive sites including military bases, airports, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies. Police have warned that the overflights could have been organised by Russian agents.

Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carry most of the country's aerial cargo.

A police spokesman told the BBC that the explosive-laden object had been spotted close to parked Antonov planes.

The detonator was removed from the explosive device. Police later carried out a controlled explosion.

Flights on the northern runway resumed at 01:55 (23:55 GMT on Tuesday). The southern runway remains closed.

Saxony's Interior Minister Armin Schuster has described the situation as as a "very serious security incident".

But Ukraine's Ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev told Welt TV: "Who else could it be but Russia?"

Similar incidents with suspicious drones in Germany have only happened since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Peter R Neumann, a professor of Security Studies at King's College London, said on X.

"Since last night, the drone war has reached Germany. And it exposes a weakness that we've known about for years," he said.

In July 2024 a parcel burst into flames on the ground at Leipzig/Halle Airport before it could be loaded onto a DHL cargo plane, one of a series of parcel fires that targeted the UK and EU countries.

The parcels had contained explosive devices that were set off by electronic timers hidden in vibrating massage pillows, according to authorities.

Last year a Chinese woman was convicted for passing on information about flight schedules and cargo movements at Leipzig/Halle Airport to a man spying for Beijing.
body.zh: 警方称，在德国机场发现了一架携带爆炸装置的无人机。 据萨克森警方称，一名员工夜间在乌克兰货机附近发现了该设备，随后莱比锡/哈勒机场部署了一个机器人。 第二个不明物体还与同一机场附近的一架货机相撞。飞机在汉诺威降落后发现有轻微损坏。 近几个月来，在军事基地、机场、能源码头、海港和物流公司等敏感地点发生一系列未经授权的无人机飞行后，德国机场处于高度戒备状态。警方警告称，这些飞越可能是俄罗斯特工组织的。 德国东部的莱比锡/哈勒机场被德国军方和北约盟国用来运输军用物资，也是乌克兰安东诺夫航空公司的基地，该航空公司运输该国大部分航空货物。 警方发言人告诉英国广播公司，在停放的安东诺夫飞机附近发现了这个充满爆炸物的物体。 雷管已从爆炸装置中取出。警方随后进行了受控爆炸。 北部跑道的航班于 01:55（格林威治标准时间周二 23:55）恢复。南部跑道仍然关闭。 萨克森州内政部长阿明·舒斯特尔将这一情况描述为“非常严重的安全事件”。 但乌克兰驻德国大使奥列克西·马基耶夫(Oleksii Makeiev)告诉世界电视台：“除了俄罗斯还能是谁？” 伦敦国王学院安全研究教授彼得·R·诺伊曼 (Peter R Neumann) 表示，自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来，德国才发生过类似的可疑无人机事件。 “从昨晚开始，无人机战争已经波及德国。它暴露了我们多年来已知的弱点，”他说。 2024 年 7 月，莱比锡/哈勒机场的一个包裹在被装上 DHL 货机之前在地面上起火，这是针对英国和欧盟国家的一系列包裹火灾之一。 据当局称，这些包裹中含有爆炸装置，这些爆炸装置是由隐藏在振动按摩枕头中的电子计时器引发的。 去年，一名中国女子因向一名为北京从事间谍活动的男子传递有关莱比锡/哈勒机场航班时刻表和货物运输的信息而被定罪。

title.en: El-Sayed's victory sends tremors through Democratic Party
title.zh: 埃尔-萨耶德的胜利在民主党内引发震动

summary.en: El-Sayed's recent victory has created significant ripples within the Democratic Party, setting the stage for a crucial general election in November where a left-wing candidate's appeal will be tested in a key swing state.
summary.zh: 埃尔-萨耶德的胜利在民主党内引发震动，为十一月的一场高风险选举奠定了基础，届时一位左翼候选人在一个摇摆州的人气将面临考验。

body.en:
The tremors from Abdul El-Sayed's victory in Michigan's Senate primary will have been felt hundreds of miles away by the Democratic Party leadership.

In a year in which Republicans appear to be facing significant electoral headwinds, Democratic primary voters have taken a chance on a left-wing insurgent, raising the stakes in a Senate race in November that could decide overall control of the upper chamber.

The question is whether the way El-Sayed has electrified the party base and tapped into their anger will work on general election voters. And whether an unabashedly left-wing Democrat can win in a swing state.

Primary results across five states on Tuesday were a snapshot of the mood of the American electorate three months before the midterm elections.

Abdul El-Sayed's victory on Tuesday night in Michigan's contentious Democratic primary race for Senate was hardly a surprise. He had led by a comfortable margin over Congresswoman Haley Stevens for weeks.

While the final projected result was much closer than those surveys had suggested, again raising questions about modern polling accuracy, it doesn't diminish the shockwaves the victory of the former Michigan health official is sending throughout the Democratic Party.

El-Sayed, the child of Egyptian immigrants, ran on a left-wing platform with the backing of such liberal stalwarts as Senators Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren and Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

Stevens had the backing of Democratic leadership in Washington, an established record as an elected official in Michigan and deep financial pockets, including $32m from Aipac -the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. Outside groups favoured her over El-Sayed by a margin of nine-to-one.

In debates and on the stump, El-Sayed proved to be the more gifted candidate, and Democrats seemed open to his policies, including government-sponsored health insurance, efforts to lower drug costs, higher taxes on the wealthy and campaign finance reform.

His campaign refrain - "money out of politics, money in your pocket" - has been a common one among left-wing candidates this election cycle.

This sets up a general election contest against former Republican Congressman Mike Rogers, who ran unopposed. It will provide perhaps the most dramatic, high-stakes test of whether a left-wing candidate can win a general election race in a true battleground state.

Given the narrowness of El-Sayed's primary victory, he has considerable work ahead if he wants to unite the party before November's vote.

While El-Sayed did well with higher-educated liberals, he'll need to win over the lower-income voters who backed Haley in Detroit and in more rural areas. These are voters whose preferences the pre-election polling did not seem to adequately...
body.zh: 周二五个州的初选结果是中期选举前三个月美国选民情绪的缩影，中期选举将决定哪个政党控制国会和主要州政府。 在共和党似乎面临重大选举阻力的一年里，民主党在密歇根州一场高风险的参议院竞选中抓住了左翼叛乱分子的机会。 全面的结果进一步证明亲以色列候选人在民主党初选中面临风险。 与此同时，唐纳德·特朗普对共和党的控制力以及他的初选支持的力量再次展现出来。 阿卜杜勒·赛义德周二晚在密歇根州颇具争议的民主党参议员初选中获胜并不令人意外。几周来，他一直以微弱优势领先国会女议员海莉·史蒂文斯。 虽然最终结果比这些调查显示的结果要接近得多，再次引发了人们对现代民意调查准确性的质疑，但这并没有减轻这位前密歇根州卫生官员的胜利给整个民主党带来的结构性震动。 埃及移民的孩子埃尔·赛义德在参议员伯尼·桑德斯、伊丽莎白·沃伦和国会女议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯等自由派坚定支持者的支持下，以毫不掩饰的进步派身份参选。 史蒂文斯得到了华盛顿民主党领导层的支持、作为密歇根州民选官员的既定记录以及雄厚的财力，其中包括来自美国以色列公共事务委员会的 3200 万美元。外部团体对她的支持率以九比一的优势战胜了埃尔赛义德。 在辩论和竞选中，埃尔-赛义德被证明是更有天赋的候选人，民主党人似乎对他的进步政策持开放态度，包括政府资助的医疗保险、降低药品成本的努力、对富人提高税收以及竞选财务改革。 他的竞选口号——“钱远离政治，钱进你的口袋”——在本次选举周期的左翼候选人中一直是常见的一句话。 这将引发一场大选，对手是前共和党众议员迈克·罗杰斯(Mike Rogers)，后者在无人反对的情况下参选。这或许将是对左翼候选人能否在真正的战场州赢得大选的最戏剧性、最高风险的考验。 鉴于埃尔赛义德的初选胜利微乎其微，如果他想在 11 月投票前团结全党，他还有大量工作要做。 虽然埃尔-赛义德在受过高等教育的自由派中表现良好，但他需要赢得底特律和更多农村地区支持黑利的低收入选民。选前民意调查似乎没有充分反映这些选民的偏好。 如果埃尔-赛义德输给罗杰斯，这可能会对民主党重新夺回控制权的希望造成致命打击……

reflection.en: A political victory can send ripples through a party, signaling a shift in direction and raising questions about future leadership. As elections approach, the character of those in authority profoundly impacts the well-being of the people they serve. Yahweh reminds us that the nature of governance directly affects the joy or sorrow of a nation.
reflection.zh: 一场政治胜利可能在党内引发涟漪，预示着方向的转变，并引发对未来领导力的疑问。随着选举临近，掌权者的品格深刻影响着他们所服务人民的福祉。雅伟提醒我们，治理的性质直接影响着一个国家的喜乐或忧愁。

title.en: India's Gen Z protest enters a new online battle
title.zh: 印度Z世代抗议进入新的网络战斗

summary.en: The streets are quiet, but a fight over the legacy of the Cockroach Janta Party movement is intensifying across Instagram, memes and social media.

body.en:
The streets are quiet, but a fight over the legacy of the Cockroach Janta Party movement is intensifying across Instagram, memes and social media.

The crowds have long dispersed from the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) main New Delhi protest site next to the Jantar Mantar.

But the CJP's 36-day campaign, which started as a satirical protest against exam leaks and grew into a wider movement voicing young Indians' anger over jobs and education, has entered a new phase.

The authorities and the CJP are now battling to shape how India's first Gen Z-led protest will be remembered.

Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25, fulfilling one of the CJP's key demands after weeks of protests that withstood tear gas and baton charges.

India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) says the minister's resignation demonstrates government accountability, while the CJP argues it was a concession won through sustained public pressure.

The BJP has mounted a coordinated online campaign aimed at reframing the movement, observers say.

MPs Bansuri Swaraj and Sambit Patra have shared videos of protesters allegedly abusing Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late mother, while Modi himself said he forgave those responsible .

Meanwhile, BJP leaders J P Nadda and Pradhan have argued that opposition parties and "anti-national forces" sought to exploit genuine student grievances for political gain.

BJP spokesperson Shazia Ilmi rejects suggestions that the party is trying to divert attention from education reform .

"A generation capable of reinventing political communication through memes and satire should not have fallen back on crude abuse," Ilmi told DW, referring to slogans directed at Modi and his late mother.

Instead of lengthy political rebuttals, they have continued to flood Instagram with memes, parody reels and remix videos that mock the BJP's attempts to appear youthful, while insisting the central issue remains education reform and accountability. 

Apar Gupta, founding director of the Internet Freedom Foundation, believes the Cockroach movement exposed a generational shift in political communication.

"Instagram is a different ecosystem," he told DW. "It rewards authenticity, personal storytelling and virality, allowing Gen Z creators to set the terms of debate before official narratives can catch up."

"Gen Z may have won the cultural conversation through reels, memes and satire, but the state still retains institutional power through takedown requests, digital surveillance and investigations," Gupta said.

"The battle is no longer just over public opinion; it is over how the protests will be remembered."

title.en: South Africa plans new rules on ex-leaders' foreign trips after Zuma's visit to India
title.zh: 南非计划制定前领导人出访新规，此前祖马曾访问印度

summary.en: South Africa is developing new regulations concerning former leaders' international travel. This initiative follows former President Jacob Zuma's recent visit to India, where he was photographed with a businessman implicated in a major corruption scandal within South Africa.
summary.zh: 南非正计划制定关于前领导人出访的新规定。此前，前总统雅各布·祖马在访问印度期间被拍到与一名据称是南非腐败丑闻核心人物的商人在一起。

body.en:
South Africa's foreign minister wants new rules and "more transparency" to apply to former heads of state undertaking foreign trips.

The recommendation to parliament follows a controversial visit to India last month by ex-President Jacob Zuma where he met one of the businessmen allegedly at the heart of a huge corruption scandal that played a role in bringing down his government.

The uproar over his meeting with Ajay Gupta prompted one minister to say that Zuma was showing the "middle finger" to South Africa .

Around a decade ago, the Gupta brothers were accused of profiting from their close links to then-President Zuma and influencing South African policy. Both parties denied wrongdoing.

The Gupta family left South Africa in 2018 after a judicial commission began investigating allegations they were involved in massive fraud, known as "state capture".

In 2022, the commission concluded that Zuma had hired and fired ministers central to the running of the country's economy at the behest of the Gupta family.

The South African authorities ended up cancelling their arrest warrant for Ajay Gupta. The two younger Gupta brothers, Atul and Rajesh, went to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where a court in 2023 turned down a South African request to extradite them

Zuma has since been expelled from the African National Congress (ANC), the party he once led, and now heads the opposition uMkhonto we Sizwe (MK).

During Zuma's visit to India, a photograph of the 84-year-old South African politician and Ajay Gupta was taken at an Indian temple.

South Africa's high commissioner to India, Anil Sooklal, was also pictured with the duo and he has since been recalled. The diplomat has denied any wrongdoing.

Foreign Affairs Minister Ronald Lamola said that his department had submitted a recommendation to parliament and the president's office for new protocols for former heads of state during foreign trips.

They would have to "provide full details" on the upcoming trip for "an informed assessment of the appropriate level of support required and any associated reputational, political, diplomatic or security risks", he said at a briefing on Wednesday.

Last year, he visited Morocco and spoke in support of the North African nation's claim over the disputed territory of Western Sahara - something South Africa opposes.

Zuma undertook the trip as MK leader but was pictured in front of the South African flag when he met Morocco's foreign minister and brought up Western Sahara.

South Africa condemned the visit and raised a formal diplomatic protest about it with Morocco.
body.zh: 南非外交部长希望新规则和“更高透明度”适用于出访的前国家元首。 在向议会提出这一建议之前，前总统雅各布·祖马上个月对印度进行了一次颇具争议的访问，他在那里会见了一名据称是巨大腐败丑闻核心人物的商人，该丑闻在导致印度政府垮台的过程中发挥了作用。 与阿贾伊·古普塔的会面引发的轩然大波促使一位部长表示，祖马正在向南非伸出“中指”。 大约十年前，古普塔兄弟被指控通过与时任总统祖马的密切关系获利并影响南非政策。双方均否认有不当行为。 2018 年，司法委员会开始调查古普塔家族涉嫌参与大规模欺诈（即“国家俘获”）的指控后，古普塔家族离开了南非。 2022年，该委员会得出结论，祖马在古普塔家族的要求下聘任和解雇了对国家经济运行至关重要的部长。 南非当局最终取消了对阿贾伊·古普塔的逮捕令。古普塔的两个弟弟阿图尔 (Atul) 和拉杰什 (Rajesh) 前往阿拉伯联合酋长国 (UAE)，当地法院于 2023 年拒绝了南非引渡他们的请求 祖马此后被他曾经领导的非洲人国民大会（ANC）开除，现在他领导反对党乌姆肯托·我们·西兹韦（MK）。 祖马访问印度期间，这位84岁的南非政治家与阿贾伊·古普塔在印度寺庙合影。 南非驻印度高级专员阿尼尔·苏克拉尔也被拍到与两人合影，此后他被召回。该外交官否认有任何不当行为。 外交部长罗纳德·拉莫拉表示，他的部门已向议会和总统办公室提交了一份建议，为前国家元首出访期间制定新的礼节。 他在周三的新闻发布会上表示，他们必须“提供即将到来的访问的全部细节”，以便“对所需的适当支持水平以及任何相关的声誉、政治、外交或安全风险进行知情评估”。 去年，他访问了摩洛哥，并发表讲话支持这个北非国家对西撒哈拉有争议领土的主权主张，而南非对此表示反对。 祖马以MK领导人的身份进行了此次访问，但当他会见摩洛哥外交部长并提到西撒哈拉时，他在南非国旗前合影。 南非谴责这次访问，并向摩洛哥提出正式外交抗议。

reflection.en: The news of South Africa's proposed rules for former leaders' foreign trips highlights the enduring impact of integrity on a nation's standing. When actions, even by those no longer in office, are linked to corruption, it can bring reproach upon a country. Striving for righteousness in public life, both past and present, is essential for a nation's honor...
reflection.zh: 南非计划制定前领导人出访新规的消息，突显了廉正对国家声誉的持久影响。当行为，即使是卸任官员的行为，与腐败挂钩时，可能给国家带来羞辱。在公共生活中，无论是过去还是现在，追求公义对于国家的尊荣和福祉至关重要。

verse.textEn: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin condemns any people.
verse.textZh: 公义使邦国高举；罪恶是人民的羞辱。

body.en:
The UN human rights chief has said he is alarmed by the rise in executions in Iran, with capital punishment continuing to be used "to instil fear among the population and suppress dissent".

Volker Türk said at least 56 people had been executed on national security-related charges since 19 March, including 27 in cases linked to January's nationwide anti-government protests.

More than 100 others were at risk of execution on similar charges, while executions for drug-related offences were also continuing at an alarming rate, he added.

Iran is thought to be the world's second-most prolific executioner after China. Last year, it put to death at least 2,159 people, according to Amnesty International.

The human rights group said that was the highest figure on record since 1981 and included 45 executions of suspected dissidents on national security-related charges.

Activists have warned that Iranian authorities might make greater use of executions against their opponents following January's protests, during which thousands of demonstrators were killed and tens of thousands were detained, and the US-Israeli war with Iran on 28 February.

In a statement, Türk urged Iranian authorities to halt all executions and move toward the abolition of the death penalty, saying that "such punishment has no place in our world".

As well as expressing alarm at the rise in executions, he said the persistent lack of fair trial and due process guarantees was "deeply troubling", with confessions allegedly obtained under torture and other ill-treatment.

"Several executions have reportedly been carried out in public. Some have reportedly been carried out only weeks after arrest," he added.

"Twelve defendants were reportedly sentenced to death following a single three-hour closed-door hearing."

There was no immediate comment from the Iranian government. But it has previously defended the use of the death penalty, saying it is limited to only "the most severe crimes".

On Monday, Iran's judiciary said it executed two men convicted of spying for Israel.

Omid Behzad and Pouria Safvat were accused of sending coordinates, images and other information on sensitive military, law enforcement and security sites to Israel's Mossad foreign intelligence service during the current war and the 12-day conflict in June 2025, according to the judiciary's Mizan news agency.

Last week, 19-year-old Arvin Kheirkhahan was executed after being convicted of the security-related charge of "enmity against God" over his alleged role in January's unrest, Iran's Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) reported, citing a source close to his family.

title.en: Hiroshima survivors warn against Japan's rearmament
title.zh: 广岛幸存者警告日本不要重新武装

summary.en: On the anniversary of the atomic bombings, survivors and activists tell DW Japan's military buildup risks eroding its longstanding commitment to pacifism.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On the anniversary of the atomic bombings, survivors and activists tell DW Japan's military buildup risks eroding its longstanding commitment to pacifism.

Japan on Thursday commemorates the 81st anniversary of the nuclear attack on  Hiroshima .

On August 6, 1945, the US dropped an atomic bomb on the Japanese city of Hiroshima during the last days of World War II , killing close to 80,000 people in the initial blast. Three days later, the US dropped a bomb over Nagasaki.

"Japan adopted a pacifist constitution in reflection on World War II," noted Masako Wada, assistant secretary general of  Nihon Hidankyo , or the Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers' Organizations. 

Japan "earned the trust of the international community as a country that promised never to wage a war again," added Wada, who survived the Nagasaki bombing as a 1-year-old.

However, in recent years, Japan has increased defense spending, eased restrictions on weapons exports and expanded the role of its military, citing growing risks from China , North Korea and Russia .

"The current administration is destroying that [trust]," Wada told DW, referring to Japan's recent efforts to pivot away from decades of strict postwar pacifism.

"Japan's recent military buildup is no different from recreating the arms race that led the country toward World War II," said 84-year-old Masashi Ieshima, who survived the Hiroshima bombing at the age of 3.

Ieshima was playing in the entrance of his house, just 1.2 miles (2 km) from the hypocenter, when the blast shattered all the windows in the house, sending shards of glass into his mother.

Seventy years later, he underwent surgery for thyroid cancer, which was officially recognized as an atomic bomb-related illness. His father, who was also exposed to the Hiroshima atomic bombing, died of laryngeal cancer.

"It makes my blood boil to see Japan justify its military buildup and the easing of arms export restrictions over the possibility of a Taiwan conflict ," said Ieshima, who serves as the chairman of Toyukai, the Tokyo affiliate of Nihon Hidankyo.

"If Japan continues down this path, it could lead to war. And if another war breaks out, I believe it will be a nuclear war." 

The average age of Japan's atomic bomb survivors, known as "hibakusha," has reached almost 87. They face the urgent challenge of passing on their testimony and calls for peace to younger generations, including their children, grandchildren, and supporters.

Takako Nakamura, a second-generation atomic bomb survivor from Nagasaki, began working actively as a family testimony speaker in February 2026, following her career retirement.

title.en: Hungary's Lake Velence is drying up
title.zh: 匈牙利韦伦采湖正在干涸

summary.en: Hungary is feeling the heat. The country's third-largest lake is shrinking, the Danube is running low, and soaring temperatures could force the country's only nuclear power plant to shut down.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Hungary is feeling the heat. The country's third-largest lake is shrinking, the Danube is running low, and soaring temperatures could force the country's only nuclear power plant to shut down.

A dead fish lies half-decayed on the shore. Its eyes have been picked out by the birds.

Hungary's  Lake Velence will likely experience a massive fish kill. That's because oxygen levels in the body of water are too low, according to environmental experts. This means more and more fish will suffocate.

Hungary has seen temperatures soar to 40 degrees Celsius, with barely any rain. This heat is having a major impact on the country's third-largest natural lake.

Its water has never been particularly deep, but the current situation is dire. Water levels have been recorded in Agard, on the southern shore, since 1933. It dropped to a historic low in September 2022, measuring just 53 centimeters. Yet as of today, August 4, the water level has dropped to a mere 29 centimeters (11 inches).

As long as it doesn't rain and temperatures remain hot, the water level will continue to drop every day, by half a centimeter per day on average. The water is currently evaporating at such a fast pace that there may soon be no continuous body of water left, only isolated pools. This could mark a critical tipping point for the lake.

The impact of Hungary's ongoing drought is already clearly visible. The lake has receded by dozens of meters. Ground once covered in water is now so dry that the soil is cracking. The reed belt surrounding the lake, which serves as a habitat for numerous bird species, is now largely rooted in dry soil.

But not all living creatures are suffering under the current conditions: that's evident from a constant hum in the air near the water's edge. As fish and aquatic plants find their habitats shrinking, flies, bacteria, and other decomposers take over, breaking down what the drought leaves behind.

The water shortage isn't just changing the lake — it's changing the entire region. Lake Velence is a popular tourist destination, located just 50 kilometers from Hungary's capital, Budapest. It is considered less crowded than nearby Lake Balaton.

But these days, there are barely any visitors. The remaining water has turned a brownish-green and taken on a slightly musty odor. A "No Swimming" sign has been put up, with yellow tape blocking access to the water. Five swimming spots have been closed to the public since July 23.

The Velence municipal government says the beach will only reopen once the lake's water quality improves, though it is unclear when that might happen. The persistent heat and low water levels mean the lake's water is getting warmer and warmer, leading to a growth in bacteria and blue-green algae.

title.en: The Australians spending their European summer waiting for a 15-minute warning
title.zh: 澳大利亚人在欧洲度过夏天等待 15 分钟警告

summary.en: More Australian aerial firefighting pilots are spending the European summers helping local authorities battle wildfires.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
While most Australians in Europe are at the beach, NSW aerial firefighting pilot Alex Pay spends his long summer days at a Greek airbase, waiting for a call to action.

"When you get a fire call, you're gonna be airborne in 15 minutes," he told SBS News.

Once in the air, Pay can spend up to 10 hours supporting local authorities in Greece's fight against wildfires, which over the past week saw two pilots killed and hundreds of thousands forced to evacuate.

Pay, 31, works for a small but growing number of Australian private aerial firefighting companies based in Western Europe during this year's fire season, which is shaping up to be the continent's worst in record.

It also comes as Australia's own looming El Niño threatens to turn up the heat on our own summer bushfire risk .

Pay is a third-generation pilot with Pay's Air Service, which is based in the NSW Hunter Region.

"I remember as a kid flying with my dad to visit my grandparents," he told SBS News.

He pilots one of 14 aircraft his company has based throughout Greece for the summer. It’s his second season in the country, and the fifth overall for his company.

They fly a variant of the Air Tractor AT-802, nicknamed the "Fire Boss" — an amphibious aircraft that scoops water into a tank, or "hopper", controlled by a computerised fire gate that can be adjusted to match exact conditions.

In Australia, there were around 130 certified firefighting aeroplane operators or individual pilots, with a further 186 helicopter operators in 2021, according to Australia's Civil Aviation Authority.

Andrew Mackay is from Ballarat-based Field Air Group, which also has planes stationed in Greece this summer supporting Pay's.

"We like to say in our industry that it's not the aircraft that put out the fires, it's the ground crew — we're merely a tool to assist them," he told SBS News.

He said pilots will often work on either side of the fire to create a "triangle or an arrowhead, so the fire comes to a point where the ground crew can then extinguish that".

Sometimes they will drop water or retardant directly onto a house under threat from a blaze.

"We spent a lot of time training and preparing scenarios that give us a good education on what we might see on the fire ground," Pay said.

On Sunday, a Greek and a Danish national were killed after two helicopters collided while fighting a fire west of Athens.

title.en: As allies desert FIFA boss Gianni Infantino, is there anyone ready to replace him?
title.zh: 随着盟友抛弃国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺，谁能取代他？

summary.en: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is facing significant controversy, leading to a loss of support from allies and questions about his future leadership.

body.en:
Pressure on FIFA president Gianni Infantino has intensified, with opposition emerging both within world football's governing body and from external critics over his since-abandoned proposal to open the World Cup to private investment.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, appointed in 2019 by Infantino as FIFA's chief of global football development, said in a statement on Tuesday that "the decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question".

His remarks followed hot on the heels of an extraordinary internal email to FIFA staff, seen by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency, in which secretary-general Mattias Grafstrom appeared to distance himself from Infantino on the issue.

Previously seen as close to Infantino, Grafstrom describes the fiasco surrounding the plan as "a sad and reproachable series of events".

FIFA floated the plan last Tuesday, saying it could raise up to US$4.2 billion ($5.95 billion) of private investment based on a valuation of US$20 billion ($28 billion) for a new commercial subsidiary, called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which it proposed would handle commercial rights for events such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

By Saturday, it was dead in the water, as Infantino announced he was abandoning the plan after widespread condemnation, with European governing body UEFA having threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the World Cup.

Far from calming the waters or shoring up his presidency, Infantino has been swamped with criticism of his leadership style; the previously smooth path to being re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term next March now looks rocky.

However, re-election is a problem down the road. For now, Infantion has others to confront.

Even though he had withdrawn the scheme, UEFA issued a letter through their lawyers in the US threatening legal action over what they had scathingly described as a "shabby, backroom, opaque deal".

"You and FIFA are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this Notice that are in your or FIFA's possession, custody, or control," its lawyer Andrew Levander said in the letter sent last Friday and seen by AFP.

Several of UEFA's member associations — Wales, Finland, Sweden and Serbia — have withdrawn their letters of support for Infantino and the English FA is strongly rumoured to be on the verge of joining them.

body.en:
Reports suggest US President Donald Trump would be "very disappointed" if Israel doesn't agree to a new peace plan for Gaza, announced last week. But how far would the US go to make that happen?

But so far the new Gaza peace deal , announced last week and meant to help end the fighting and ease the ongoing humanitarian crisis in the coastal enclave, only seems to have resulted in another standoff between the key belligerents.

However, experts point out, there are some differences between this new peace deal and previous arrangements that could be positive.

For one thing, it is much more detailed and substantive. For another, statements by Trump indicate he might be more willing to push Israel towards accepting the deal. And finally, after resisting the idea for years, this month the Gaza-based group Hamas has agreed to disarm.

It was Hamas that sent fighters into Israel on October 7, 2023, an attack that resulted in over 1,000 deaths and sparked nearly three years of an ongoing Israeli military campaign in Gaza. The Israeli military has since killed over 73,000 people there , causing a UN independent commission of inquiry to classify its behavior as a genocide.

One of the main sticking points of any peace plan for Gaza has been the sequencing of events. Israel has demanded that Hamas disarm before it withdraws its troops from Gaza. But up until last month, Hamas had refused to disarm until Israel withdrew its troops. This led to an ongoing stalemate.

Early in July, Hamas agreed to hand over power to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza , or NCAG, a group of independent technocrats set up to govern Gaza. Later in July, the group also agreed to hand over their weapons to the NCAG.

Hamas agreeing to disarm after years of promoting armed resistance against Israel should be taken seriously, says Muhammad Shehada, a visiting fellow with the Middle East and North Africa program at the European Council of Foreign Affairs, who is originally from Gaza .

Hamas has been under pressure from negotiators from other countries like Egypt and Qatar and this could also be something of a political tactic "to expose that Israel is the party that is obstructing any progress in Gaza under [Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu's government," Shehada concedes.

But, he added, "they would not have made such a major, historic concession unless their backs were totally against the wall and they fully understood that this is the only way forward."

Should Israel agree to the new peace plan, there would also be no way Hamas could renege.

body.en:
Spain's interior minister headed into a tense face-off with EU counterparts on Tuesday, as the bloc sought to draw lessons from an influx of migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in hastily arranged video talks.

The unprecedented sight of an estimated 60,000 people streaming into Ceuta from Morocco — dozens died in the attempt and almost all have since left — exposed the fault lines on migration among EU nations.

Since images first emerged of the mass arrivals, most of whom swam around a barrier separating the enclave from Morocco, the Spanish government has found itself pitted against many of its EU partners.

The bloc's interior ministers dialled in for a videoconference that could provide a chance to look for common ground — but looked equally likely to set the stage for a showdown.

While Spain moved swiftly to send migrants back from Ceuta — where it said an estimated 2,500 remained as of Monday — the government of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez backs a more open approach to migration than most of its EU counterparts.

Countries pushing a harder line are led most vocally by Italy — whose Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has attacked Madrid's stance, and specifically a recent push to grant legal status to undocumented migrants already in the country.

Both Italy and Denmark last week advocated suspending Spain from the Schengen free-travel area over the Ceuta crisis — a notion firmly rejected by Madrid, and which in any case is legally impossible under EU rules.

In a letter to the heads of the EU's institutions Saturday, Sanchez accused fellow EU countries of having "selfish" attitudes and called for emergency talks to work on a "common response" to such incidents.

Within hours, 22 countries led by Italy, Denmark, Germany and Hungary sent a counter-letter also demanding urgent talks, but with a different goal: to continue pressing their tough stance on immigration.

In a taste of what to expect, preparatory talks among the bloc's EU ambassadors on Monday saw Spain's envoy voice "frustration" with a perceived lack of support from fellow capitals, one EU diplomat told the Agence-France Presse (AFP) news agency.

Conversely — while all assured Madrid of their "solidarity" — some member states "are asking themselves if recent policies adopted by Spain have not sent the signal that the doors are open", added the diplomat.

The EU has significantly tightened its migration rules in recent months, including by allowing member states to send failed asylum seekers to so-called "return hubs" located outside the bloc's borders.

title.en: 'Urgent' call for military build-up in Australia's backyard amid Chinese, Russian threats

summary.en: Tensions are escalating in the Pacific region, prompting one nation to significantly increase its military capabilities due to growing distrust among key international actors.

body.en:
Japan needs to boost its military with a "sense of urgency and crisis", its defence minister said on Tuesday, as a new government assessment reiterated growing risks posed by China, North Korea, and Russia.

Japan is already beefing up military spending and security cooperation in Asia, deploying missile launchers to outer islands, moving to acquire "counter-strike" capabilities, and easing rules on weapons exports.

But Shinjiro Koizumi said in a preface to the annual defence white paper that it was "imperative that Japan further reinforce and transform its defence capabilities with a stronger sense of urgency and crisis than ever before".

In the Asia-Pacific, "not only are China and North Korea further strengthening their military capabilities, China-Russia and Russia-North Korea are also reinforcing their cooperation", he added.

The new white paper said China was "intensifying its activities" in the region around Japan, "extending beyond the so-called first island chain to the second island chain".

It listed a series of incidents in 2025, including activities by Chinese aircraft carriers and the "unusual close approach" by Chinese aircraft to Japanese planes in two incidents in June and July.

Japanese jets scrambled 595 times in the year to 31 March 2026, including 366 sorties against Chinese aircraft and 214 for Russian planes.

Japan decided in April to lift its self-imposed ban on weapons exports, but the white paper highlighted problems in the country's production base that could jeopardise procurement and innovation.

Koizumi also said that he and US counterpart Pete Hegseth had "exchanged candid views" on the "unwavering" US-Japan alliance, while also increasing security cooperation with the Philippines, Australia, and South Korea to realise a "a free and open Indo-Pacific".

"As the security environment becomes increasingly and rapidly severe, what is required now is to strengthen resilience against crises all across the entire Indo-Pacific region," Koizumi said.

"In order to do so Japan will build and expand multilayered networks among allies and like-minded countries, and enhance interconnectivity with like-minded countries and others in every area."

The link between defence and future prosperity comes as Takaichi's administration prepares a new national security strategy.

Military experts expect it to call for further spending increases aimed primarily at deterring China from starting a conflict with Taiwan that could also draw Japan into a prolonged war.

body.zh: 日本防卫大臣周二表示，日本需要以“紧迫感和危机感”增强其军事实力，因为新的政府评估重申了中国、朝鲜和俄罗斯构成的日益增长的风险。 日本已经在加强亚洲的军费开支和安全合作，在外岛部署导弹发射器，努力获得“反恐”能力，并放宽武器出口规则。 但小泉进次郎在年度防卫白皮书的序言中表示，“日本必须以前所未有的紧迫感和危机感，进一步强化和转变防卫能力”。 他补充说，在亚太地区，“不仅中国和朝鲜进一步加强军事实力，中俄、俄朝合作也在加强”。 新的白皮书称，中国正在日本周边地区“加强活动”，“范围从所谓的第一岛链延伸到第二岛链”。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 它列出了2025年的一系列事件，包括中国航母的活动以及中国飞机在6月和7月的两起事件中“异常接近”日本飞机。 截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日的一年中，日本战机紧急升空 595 次，其中针对中国飞机出动 366 架次，针对俄罗斯飞机出动 214 架次。 日本四月份决定解除自行实施的武器出口禁令，但白皮书强调了该国生产基地可能危及采购和创新的问题。 小泉纯一郎还表示，他和美国外长皮特·赫格斯就“坚定不移”的美日同盟“坦诚交换了意见”，同时还加强了与菲律宾、澳大利亚和韩国的安全合作，以实现“自由开放的印太”。 小泉说：“随着安全环境迅速变得日益严峻，现在需要的是加强整个印太地区应对危机的抵御能力。” 为此，日本将在盟友和志同道合的国家之间建立和扩大多层网络，并在各个领域加强与志同道合的国家和其他国家的互联互通。” 国防与未来繁荣之间的联系正值高市政府准备新的国家安全战略之际。 军事专家预计，它将呼吁进一步增加开支，主要目的是阻止中国与台湾发生冲突，这也可能将日本拖入一场旷日持久的战争。 中国对日本回归“新军国主义”表示震惊，自日本鹰派新首相上台以来，两国关系不断恶化。

summary.en: The article argues that democracy is jeopardized when human leaders unwisely place their trust in artificial intelligence. It highlights the critical need for enlightened leadership, particularly from the US president, to advocate for global AI regulation, contrasting this need with current political realities.
summary.zh: 文章指出，当人类领导者不明智地将信任寄托于人工智能时，民主就会受到威胁。它强调了开明领导人（特别是美国总统）推动全球人工智能监管的迫切需求，并将其与当前的政治现实进行了对比。

body.en: We need an enlightened US president to make the case for global AI regulation. Donald Trump is the exact opposite of what is needed When I am woken by the sound of my dog whining, I understand that she is hungry and wants me to get up. When my alarm clock goes off, I don’t consider its needs. It is following an instruction to rouse me at a certain time but it doesn’t care if I stay in bed. It doesn’t try to get me up by other means. The dog, on the other hand, will go to plan B. She barks. This capacity for autonomous action was once a difference between animals and machines. AI has blurred the line . Advanced models devise their own strategies to reach a goal. The task might be defined by a human master, but the machine weighs its options for delivery. It can make its own choices. Given rules, it can break them. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我们需要一位开明的美国总统来为全球人工智能监管提供理由。唐纳德·特朗普与我们所需要的恰恰相反。当我被狗的哀鸣声吵醒时，我知道她饿了，想让我起床。当我的闹钟响起时，我不会考虑它的需求。它会按照指令在特定时间叫醒我，但它并不关心我是否留在床上。它不会试图通过其他方式让我起床。另一方面，狗会执行 B 计划。她会吠叫。这种自主行动的能力曾经是动物和机器之间的区别。人工智能已经模糊了界限。先进的模型会制定自己的策略来实现目标。该任务可能由人类主人定义，但机器会权衡其交付选项。它可以做出自己的选择。既定规则，它可能会打破它们。继续阅读...

verse.textZh: 你要专心仰赖雅伟，不可倚靠自己的聪明。

body.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed our destinies for ever. We have been in love since we were teenagers, and today we are happily married – all because I accidentally discovered a forbidden novel in someone else’s house. It was a hot summer’s evening in 2009, in Kumul, Xinjiang. I was 16 and my father insisted I accompany him to visit a distant relative, where they would spend hours chatting about the old days and feasting as if they hadn’t eaten in years. As the well-behaved teenager I tried to be, I sat politely, nodding at their stories and pretending to absorb their “life lessons”, attempting to hide my boredom. The living room, with its small windows and bright lighting, was unbearable. Continue reading...

summary.en: Recent advancements in China's artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing, and robotics technologies have caused significant disruption in global financial markets and the US tech industry.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

body.zh: 从中华帝国到当今的印度，学生运动不断地采用他们那个时代的工具和符号来挑战权威。 2026 年 7 月 22 日，在多雨的印度孟买，一名穿着休闲的年轻女子走到一辆载着被拘留学生的缓慢行驶的警车前。她将手掌放在引擎盖上，迫使车辆停了下来。 手机从各个角度捕捉了这一时刻。她也举起了自己的手机，记录了这次遭遇。几个小时内，这段视频就传遍了印度及其他地区。 它成为蟑螂简塔党抗议活动的标志性视觉效果之一，在印度医学入学考试泄密后，学生们在这场运动中要求透明度和问责制。 但这一刻的​​力量不仅在于她所做的事情，还在于她的所作所为很快被人们看到。一个年轻女子对抗权威的一个动作，成为了数百万屏幕上共享的符号。 虽然这段视频属于在社交媒体上长大的一代人，但其背后的冲动却要古老得多。 从法庭请愿书和革命海报到照片、雨伞和模因，学生运动不断地调整他们可用的工具和符号，将它们变成异议的工具。 早在电视或社交媒体跨境传播异议之前，学生们就已经找到了表达不满的方法。 例如，在中国东汉，太学的学者与具有改革思想的官员结盟，反对宫廷中有权有势的宦官，许多人认为宦官腐败且在政治上专横。 他们通过公开批评、政治网络和请愿来表达他们的反对意见。 在政治沟通通过官方渠道进行的时代，请愿是向王室表达不满的既定方式之一。它们以正式语言编写并通过官僚机构传达，将学生的担忧直接传达到国家的沟通系统中。 1968 年的巴黎，学生们挑战大学当局和保守的战后社会秩序。随着示威活动在法国首都蔓延并吸引了工人，该运动最持久的贡献之一来自巴黎美术学院的一个地下室工作室。 Atelier Populaire（“人民工作室”）在抗议期间印制了数千张海报，其中许多是在一夜之间印制的。他们大胆的图形、轮廓和口号成为了这场运动的视觉语言。许多作品都是集体制作的，没有作者的名字，这有助于将抗议转变为公众的共同声音。 这些海报及其信息可能会在一夜之间出现在数十个地方，使抗议活动在当地得到广泛的关注。 当图像可以跨境传输时，抗议的影响力也变得更大。 在...

Yahweh, through the prophet Amos, calls for justice to flow powerfully and consistently, reminding us that true righteousness should be an undeniable force in society. This pursuit of a more just world often requires courage to speak truth to...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

summary.en: Jean-Claude Perrottet was questioned at the Operation Rosny hearings about the actions of the NSW Liberals’ hard-right Reformers faction Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast It’s perhaps inevitable that in a large family there might be one member who is a...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
It’s perhaps inevitable that in a large family there might be one member who is a bit of a wild card.

It’s more problematic when that family has a distinctive surname and one is a public figure.

Dominic Perrottet has 12 siblings – and his younger brother Jean-Claude Perrottet has an uncanny ability to attract headlines.

On Wednesday, Jean-Claude was the star witness at the Independent Commission against Corruption . It is investigating allegations that illegal donations were used to fund branch stacking within the NSW Liberal party by a shadowy organisation known as the Reformers, of which Jean-Claude was a key figure.

In 2017 Jean-Claude, then aged 20, was found not guilty of rape in the NSW district court.

The charges stemmed from an alcohol-charged incident with a 19-year old woman following an end-of-year formal at St John’s College, Sydney University in 2015. The jury took less than two hours to find Perrottet not guilty.

Rape cases sometimes get reported in the normal course, but because Dominic was then the youthful NSW treasurer in the Berejiklian government and the safety of women on campus was a subject of live public debate, it was regarded as highly newsworthy.

By 2018, Jean-Claude Perrottet was doing a commerce degree at the University of NSW and had found employment with conservative Catholic parliamentarians. First it was in Damien Tudehope’s electorate office, then with upper house MP David Clarke, then in 2019, back to Tudehope in his ministerial office.

He might have been a mere 21-year-old staffer, but Jean-Claude still made headlines.

In 2019, the Sydney Morning Herald published articles about an alleged concerted effort by facets of the Liberal party’s hard right to undermine sitting members in several safe state and federal seats in Sydney’s north-west.

The stories named Jean-Claude and fellow staffer Christian Ellis who were both employed at the time by Tudehope, then the minister for small business.

That was the first time we heard of the NSW Reformers, a conservative group of Catholics alleged to be behind the stacking.

Despite trying to operate covertly, the Reformers have refused to fade into obscurity.

In 2022 Liberal state MP Ray Williams, one of the Reformers’ targets, used a late night speech in parliament to raise allegations about the Reformers’ activities.

This must have been challenging for Dominic Perrottet. He would have known that, at the very least, Icac would likely question his little brother.

Kmart recently launched a new accessory — dubbed Camera Glasses — which it said blends stylish eyewear with built-in camera technology.

At a glance, the black-framed spectacles from Kmart's in-house brand Anko look like any ordinary pair of glasses. But by Monday 3 August, there were reports the product was sold out online.

At $89, the glasses provide a low-cost alternative to the smart glasses designed by glasses company Ray-Ban and Facebook owners Meta, which start at $337. The latest generation of this technology costs more than $700.

A recent promotional video for Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses, featuring celebrity Kylie Jenner, showcased its features. Those include an ultra-HD camera, discreet open-ear Bluetooth speakers, and translation technology.

In July, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said people who don't wear smart glasses in the future will be at a "pretty significant cognitive disadvantage".

But she said: "If the price is cheaper ... if you're not paying at the bridge, you may pay at the toll.

"We still need to ask ourselves, this data that we're essentially generating for these companies; how is it being handled, by whom and at what cost?"

Stilinovic also said wearable technology, regardless of its price point, raises complex questions around privacy and security.

Depending on the product, they may have AI-enabled programs embedded, which analyse human behaviours including eye movements, head tracking and voice patterns.

"They are picking up data of where you're walking around, the space that you're in, what you're doing at particular times ... even to the extent of knowing the map out of your home," Stilinovic said.

Facial recognition technology is not active in most smart glasses on the market.

However, in 2024, students from Harvard University combined smart glasses, facial search engines, AI language tools and public databases to test surveillance capabilities. They found information including a person's home address, name and phone number — just by looking at them.

title.en: The Australians spending their European summer waiting for a 15-minute warning
title.zh: 澳大利亚人正在欧洲度过夏季，等待15分钟的火情警报

summary.en: Australian aerial firefighting pilots are increasingly spending their European summers assisting local authorities in combating wildfires, often waiting for short-notice deployment.
summary.zh: 越来越多的澳大利亚空中消防飞行员在欧洲夏季帮助当地政府扑灭野火，他们常常在等待短时间通知后立即投入工作。

body.en:
While most Australians in Europe are at the beach, NSW aerial firefighting pilot Alex Pay spends his long summer days at a Greek airbase, waiting for a call to action.

"When you get a fire call, you're gonna be airborne in 15 minutes," he told SBS News.

Once in the air, Pay can spend up to 10 hours supporting local authorities in Greece's fight against wildfires, which over the past week saw two pilots killed and hundreds of thousands forced to evacuate.

Pay, 31, works for a small but growing number of Australian private aerial firefighting companies based in Western Europe during this year's fire season, which is shaping up to be the continent's worst in record.

It also comes as Australia's own looming El Niño threatens to turn up the heat on our own summer bushfire risk .

Pay is a third-generation pilot with Pay's Air Service, which is based in the NSW Hunter Region.

"I remember as a kid flying with my dad to visit my grandparents," he told SBS News.

He pilots one of 14 aircraft his company has based throughout Greece for the summer. It’s his second season in the country, and the fifth overall for his company.

They fly a variant of the Air Tractor AT-802, nicknamed the "Fire Boss" — an amphibious aircraft that scoops water into a tank, or "hopper", controlled by a computerised fire gate that can be adjusted to match exact conditions.

In Australia, there were around 130 certified firefighting aeroplane operators or individual pilots, with a further 186 helicopter operators in 2021, according to Australia's Civil Aviation Authority.

Andrew Mackay is from Ballarat-based Field Air Group, which also has planes stationed in Greece this summer supporting Pay's.

"We like to say in our industry that it's not the aircraft that put out the fires, it's the ground crew — we're merely a tool to assist them," he told SBS News.

He said pilots will often work on either side of the fire to create a "triangle or an arrowhead, so the fire comes to a point where the ground crew can then extinguish that".

Sometimes they will drop water or retardant directly onto a house under threat from a blaze.

"We spent a lot of time training and preparing scenarios that give us a good education on what we might see on the fire ground," Pay said.

On Sunday, a Greek and a Danish national were killed after two helicopters collided while fighting a fire west of Athens.

title.en: Jetstar’s new overhead baggage rules explained: When they start and what you'll pay
title.zh: 捷星航空新随身行李规定解读：何时生效，费用几何

summary.en: Budget airline Jetstar is changing its carry-on baggage policy, moving from a weight-based limit to a new model based on size. This adjustment will affect when the new rules start and what passengers will be charged.
summary.zh: 廉价航空公司捷星航空将更改其随身行李政策，从基于重量的限制转向基于尺寸的新模式。这项调整将影响新规何时生效以及乘客需要支付的费用。

body.en:
Storing carry-on baggage in overhead lockers on Jetstar flights will cost up to $52 one-way, as the budget airline announces new charges for passengers.

Jetstar chief executive Stephanie Tully says the changes to the airline's carry-on baggage allowances will streamline boarding and help more flights depart on time.

"Our new carry-on baggage model provides more choice to customers while helping to keep our fares low," Tully added.

"You only pay for what you need — travelling with less means paying less, and you can always add more if you need."

The changes follow "extensive research and feedback from customers and crew" which found frustrations with weighing bags and finding enough room in overhead lockers, Jetstar said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

From 2 February, Jetstar will lift its 7kg carry-on weight limit in favour of a size-based carry-on baggage model.

Cabin baggage scales used to weigh passengers' carry-on bags before boarding will no longer be "routinely" used, the airline said.

Passengers will be able to bring one small bag to place under the seat, such as a backpack, handbag or laptop bag. That bag can weigh up to 10kg and be up to 40 x 30 x 20cm. Any bags larger than that will incur a fee.

Passengers who want to store a larger carry-on bag in overhead lockers will be charged between $25 and $52 one-way, depending on the flight route, for "limited" priority carry-on.

Jetstar said the fee for a one-way flight from Launceston to Sydney would start at $25, rising to $33 for a one-way flight between Sydney and Melbourne and $52 for a one-way flight between Cairns and Tokyo.

Priority boarding will be provided for passengers who pay for the carry-on option.

If you're travelling with an infant, you can bring an extra under-the-seat bag at no extra cost.

body.en:
Ruby and her 11-year-old son Mark were dreading the day his scores on the national school assessment program were released.

And they confirmed the family's worst fears: despite working hard to learn, the Year 5 student remained behind his peers.

Mark, whose name the Australian Associated Press agreed not to publish, was one of more than 1.3 million children in Years 3, 5, 7, and 9 who sat the National Assessment Program — Literacy and Numeracy (NAPLAN) in 2026.

As the only standardised national assessment, NAPLAN was primarily designed to help governments and schools measure results and fix funding or teaching shortfalls.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"When I got the results, because it comes under Mark's name, he wanted to see his results,'' Ruby said.

"I just thought to myself, 'How could it be right at the bottom when he's improved so much?'"

But scores for reading were worse than in 2025 for every year level, and Year 5 students were the only cohort whose writing ability had improved.

Overall, about one in three students across all levels did not meet basic literacy and numeracy benchmarks, falling into "developing" and "needs additional support" categories.

The writing scores were a particular concern in the two lowest grades tested, with less than 10 per cent of students exceeding national benchmarks.

Numeracy results had improved for most cohorts since 2025, though Year 3's score had decreased.

Results from previous years showed a clear literacy divide between children from wealthy, educated areas and those who grow up in areas of low socio-economic status.

Ruby said she also struggled at school and her challenges went unnoticed because of her learning environment.

"With Mark, I just wish there was more people, just more at the school to help," she said.

Better support that understands the specific needs of struggling families would help improve results, The Smith Family chief executive Doug Taylor said.

"With 72,000 low-income students across Australia, the right support at the right time can make a huge difference," he said, noting schools should also consider the skills students had beyond academic ones.

In rural communities and towns with high Indigenous populations, results have dramatically improved in recent years.

That was due to increased funding and the use of explicit teaching models, Education Minister Jason Clare said in a speech at the Garma Indigenous festival over the weekend.

"Over the last four years, the numeracy results of Indigenous students have gone up and up,'' he said.

title.en: 2026 Census: The new questions on gender and sexual orientation explained

summary.en: Gender identity, sexuality and ancestry: Here's what's new in the 2026 Census.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Census of Population and Housing has long tracked a changing Australia — but for more than a century, a piece of the nation's story has been missing, LGBTIQ+ Health Australia CEO Nicky Bath says.

Bath says the organisation has been calling for the addition of questions regarding sexual orientation, gender identification and expression.

"I remember in the run-up to the 2021 Census being contacted by older people who thought that they wouldn't be alive for the 2026 Census, and it was very sad for them that they wouldn't be able to participate ... in this way," she told SBS News.

The 2026 Census will now include two new questions about gender and sexual orientation.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Respondents will still be asked about their sex recorded at birth, but people over the age of 16 can also specify their gender as male, female, non-binary or another term.

An optional question regarding sexual orientation has been added, with answers including straight, gay or lesbian, bisexual or an open-ended response for another term.

Bath said Census data — which will be released in three phases starting from June 2027 — will inform the availability, funding and location of LGBTQI+ community and health services.

"The decision has been a long time coming ... for many people, being able to mark those boxes in the Census is really important with regards to validation and for us to be seen as important members of the community. That's a really important historical moment."

Advocates like Equality Australia say the number of people living in houseboats has been recorded in the Census for decades, but LGBTQI+ populations have not been traced.

Anna Brown, CEO of Equality Australia, said Census data collected about LGBTQI+ people would be "transformative".

"We're really looking forward to learning just how many LGBTQ+ people there are in Australia, because we know that if we aren't counted, we remain invisible in the data that shapes decisions about our lives," she told SBS News.

"Better data leads to better decisions on health, housing, education, aged care, and community services. Until now, governments have been making these decisions without a complete picture of our communities."

Brown has also called for Australians with innate variations of sex characteristics or intersex people to be counted by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

"We will continue to advocate for its inclusion and work with the ABS ... towards recommending that this population be included," she said.

Census questions are informed by the 2020 ABS standards for sex, gender, variations in sex characteristics, and sexual orientation variables....
